problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 7 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 4 & 3 & -12 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 7 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 7 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 4 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-7{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 4 & 3 & -12 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-7{C}_{3}.$
